summary: Arithmetic Nielsen-core surfaces of area π times a minus continued-fraction period equidistribute by genus on the modular orbifold. The three-sign Hecke and half-weight trace identities connect surface integrals, geodesics and CM points. This 158-item checkpoint records pinned imports, owner-specific missing contracts, normalization corrections, a phase-uniqueness counterexample and eight explicit recursive source/proof gates; it does not certify complete closure.

items.name: Rankin–Selberg norm identity and the norm comparison for spectral summation
items.statement: Let φ(z)=2√y Σ_{n≠0} a(n)K_{ir}(2π|n|y)e(nx) be an even Hecke–Maass cusp form for PSL₂(Z) with Laplace eigenvalue 1/4+r², normalized by a(1)=1 as in (5.7), so that L(s,φ)=Σa(n)n^{−s}=∏_p(1−a(p)p^{−s}+p^{−2s})^{−1} as in (5.8), and let ⟨φ,φ⟩=∫_F|φ|²y^{−2}dxdy. Then ⟨φ,φ⟩=2L(1,sym²φ)/cosh(πr). Consequently ||φ||₂cosh²(πr/4)≤√2·L(1,sym²φ)^{1/2}, and L(1,sym²φ)≪_ε r^{2+ε} (r≥1), so ||φ||₂cosh²(πr/4)≪_ε r^{1+ε}.
proofSteps: Unfold against E(z,s)=Σ_{Γ∞\Γ}Im(γz)^s of (5.2) for Re s>1: ∫_F|φ|²E(z,s)dμ=∫_0^∞∫_0^1|φ|²y^{s−2}dxdy=8(2π)^{−s}Σ_{n≥1}a(n)²n^{−s}·∫_0^∞K_{ir}(u)²u^{s−1}du, using a(−n)=a(n) and real a(n).
Mellin integral: ∫_0^∞K_{ir}(u)²u^{s−1}du=2^{s−3}Γ(s/2)²Γ(s/2+ir)Γ(s/2−ir)/Γ(s); at s=1 this is (1/4)·π·|Γ(1/2+ir)|²=π²/(4cosh πr).
Hecke relations give Σ_{n≥1}a(n)²n^{−s}=ζ(s)L(s,sym²φ)/ζ(2s) (Rankin–Selberg), with residue L(1,sym²φ)/ζ(2)=6L(1,sym²φ)/π² at s=1.

Res_{s=1}E(z,s)=3/π=1/vol(F) for dμ=y^{−2}dxdy; since φ is cuspidal, Res_{s=1}∫_F|φ|²E dμ=(3/π)⟨φ,φ⟩. Comparing residues: (3/π)⟨φ,φ⟩=8(2π)^{−1}·(6L(1,sym²φ)/π²)·π²/(4cosh πr)=(6/π)L(1,sym²φ)/cosh(πr).
For x≥0, √2cosh²(x/4)/√(cosh x)≤√2 (maximum at x=0, limit 1/2 as x→∞), so ||φ||₂cosh²(πr/4)=√(2L(1,sym²φ))·cosh²(πr/4)/√(cosh πr)≤√2·L(1,sym²φ)^{1/2}.

Bessel bound. For u>0 and r≥1, K_{ir}(u)=½∫_{−∞}^{∞}e^{−u cosh t+irt}dt (DLMF 10.32.9). Shifting the contour to Im t=θ∈(0,π/2), where |e^{−u cosh(t+iθ)}|=e^{−u cosh(Re t)cos θ} decays, gives |K_{ir}(u)|≤e^{−rθ}K₀(u cos θ). Take θ=π/2−1/r, so cos θ=sin(1/r)≥2/(πr): |K_{ir}(u)|≤e^{1−πr/2}K₀(2u/(πr)). Checked numerically for r∈[1,40], u∈[0.01,80], with ratio at most 0.70.

Hecke bound, uniform in φ. T_p has operator norm at most p^{1/2}+p^{−1/2} on L²(Γ\H), so |a(p)|≤p^{1/2}+p^{−1/2}. The recursion a(p^{k+1})=a(p)a(p^k)−a(p^{k−1}) gives |a(p^k)|≤(k+1)(p^{1/2}+p^{−1/2})^k, hence |a(n)|≤d(n)n^{1/2}∏_{p^k‖n}(1+1/p)^k≪_ε n^{1/2+ε}.

Norm bound. F⊂{|x|≤1/2, y≥√3/2}, and Parseval in x gives ∫_{−1/2}^{1/2}|φ|²dx=8yΣ_{n≥1}a(n)²K_{ir}(2πny)². So ⟨φ,φ⟩≤8Σ_n a(n)²∫_{√3/2}^∞K_{ir}(2πny)²dy/y≤8e²e^{−πr}Σ_n a(n)²J(2√3n/r), with J(c)=∫_c^∞K₀(v)²dv/v. Here J(c)≪(1+log(1/c))³ for c≤1 and J(c)≪e^{−2c} for c≥1.

Summing with the Hecke bound, Σ_{n≤r}n^{1+2ε}(1+log(r/n))³+Σ_{n>r}n^{1+2ε}e^{−4√3n/r}≪_ε r^{2+3ε}. Hence ⟨φ,φ⟩≪_ε r^{2+ε}e^{−πr}, and by the identity L(1,sym²φ)=⟨φ,φ⟩cosh(πr)/2≪_ε r^{2+ε}. With the previous step, ||φ||₂cosh²(πr/4)≪_ε r^{1+ε}. No GL₃ theory is needed.

Checks: the Mellin integral agrees with π²/(4cosh πr) to 40 digits at r=0.5, 2, 5; the paper's example on p.966 gives L(1,sym²φ)≈1.1477; the contour-shift Bessel bound was checked numerically. routes.title: Fuchsian groups and orbifold Riemann surfaces, Part II: Nielsen cores and quadratic-class surfaces
routes.reason: The upstream roadmap supplies Fuchsian actions, polygon and orbifold infrastructure, but its reviewed audit does not supply this arithmetic convex-core construction. Extend it, never replace or re-plan its layers.
routes.brief: Import Fuchsian groups and orbifold Riemann surfaces (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/FuchsianOrbifolds), especially its polygon theorem and effective PSL action; import the arithmetic class/cycle dictionary from Geometry of numbers and quadratic arithmetic (GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.3), and genus signs from Multiquadratic fields and genus theory (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Multiquadratic) with MultiquadraticPartII. For each narrow ideal class A of a positive fundamental discriminant D, construct the finite-area Nielsen core F_A and its locally isometric map to the modular orbifold. For the primitive minus period of length ℓ_A, prove signature (0; ℓ_A copies of 2; one cusp; one geodesic boundary), free product Z*(C2)^ℓ_A, simple geodesic boundary projecting to C_A of length 2 log ε_D, area πℓ_A, and the conformal invariance/class identification asserted in Theorem 1. Include free-side endpoint ordering, limit-set convex hull, cyclic-presentation invariance, complementary tiles and the exact multiplicity cover. Define integration by pushforward of the upstairs core measure; retain multiplicity where the modular projection overlaps itself. Prove the truncated Stokes conversion with compatible orientation and horizontal-side decay, importing the Laplacian and cusp estimates from Automorphic spectral theory (AutomorphicSpectralTheory). Theorem 2 is owned by GN.4 and imports these measures; it is not a second analytic endpoint here. Every construction needs its stated API and tests, including D=12 and D=28 and the all-2 parabolic rejection. S2 still requires source-level proof closure before design acceptance.

routes.title: Multiquadratic fields and genus theory, Part II: real quadratic signs and form characters
routes.reason: All four audited upstream genus-theory layers are built. These items are specific extensions/adapters for the real-quadratic surface argument; the class group, elementary quotient, genus characters, rank formula and principal genus theorem remain imported.
routes.brief: Import Multiquadratic fields and genus theory (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Multiquadratic) and the existing NumberField.NarrowClassGroup, elementary-two quotient, prime-discriminant factorization, genus characters and principal genus theorem. Extend these with J²=1 and ker(Cl⁺→Cl)={1,J}, equal sizes of genus cosets, and χ(J)=sgn(d) for a genus factorization D=dd′; include the criterion that all genus characters are even precisely when the discriminant is a sum of two squares in the paper’s stated sense. Construct the character χ_d(Q) for possibly imprimitive integral quadratic forms by a represented value prime to d, with the zero case gcd(a,b,c,d)>1, and prove representative independence and proper-equivalence invariance. Import the oriented form carrier and content reduction from Geometry of numbers and quadratic arithmetic (GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.3). The consumers are Hecke period factorization in Analytic number theory (AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4), plus-space trace identities in Metaplectic automorphic forms (MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.7), and genus equidistribution in GN.4. Do not re-plan any of the built upstream algebra, assign quadratic-form reduction here, or assert class-number-one infinitude. Tests must include D=12, discriminant factors at 2, the trivial d=1 character, imprimitive forms and the distinction between Cl⁺/Cl⁺² and Cl⁺[2]. S3 and S5 record the remaining source obligations.
